claims.text: Nickel-based alloy components will significantly reduce corrosion relative to traditional materials in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Nickel-based alloy components will extend equipment service life relative to traditional materials.
The proposed nickel-based alloy has resistance to corrosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
The proposed nickel-based alloy is stable at the operating temperature of the hot-dip aluminum process.
The nickel-based alloy forms a protective oxide layer during exposure to high-temperature liquid aluminum.
The protective oxide layer prevents direct contact between liquid aluminum and the underlying alloy.
Preventing direct contact between liquid aluminum and the underlying alloy reduces the corrosion rate.
After prolonged exposure to high-temperature liquid aluminum, nickel-based alloy components will exhibit significantly less wear than traditional materials.
